title: Ordinary affine-line homotopy invariance for finite twists
statement:
Fix the finite datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ for $n\geq1$, and the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with their finite small-etale realizations of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].  Let $X$ be an arbitrary $k$-scheme and let $p:\mathbf A^1_X\to X$ be the affine-line projection of [def-sbc-affine-space] (relative dimension one).  Use ordinary sheaf cohomology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (zero in negative degrees for a sheaf) on the small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-derived-direct-image] in the respective topologies. For every integer $r$, the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]
$$
 A(r)_X\longrightarrow Rp_*A(r)_{\mathbf A^1_X}
$$
is an isomorphism on the small etale site and on the small pro-etale site (for the etale-origin finite twist).  Consequently, for every integer $q$, pullback $p^*:H^q(X,A(r))\to H^q(\mathbf A^1_X,A(r))$ is an isomorphism in either topology.  These isomorphisms are natural in $X$ and in finite coefficient maps, and the etale and pro-etale isomorphisms are identified by the canonical comparison.

source.place: Clause (a), Reduction to a geometric fibre, and Coefficients: arbitrary-base and all-twists refinement of the ordinary affine-line acyclicity input, needed in the shear paragraph of main-20261015/sk-prop-an/lem-pur-frame-independence.proof.md. This new statement is agent-formulated; the unit itself states the finite-type case.

proof.text:
Put $m=\ell^n$. In the valuation-ring description of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$ and $mA=0$; $A$ is finite. Here is an explicit reading of the finite twist in either topology. Put $M_T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](2), $M_T\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}}(\mathbf Z/m)_T\cong\mu_{m,T}$; clause (3) of the same node for $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\varpi_E=\ell$ (so that $\mathcal O_E(1)_T=M_T$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathbf Z/m$) identifies this with $M_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(\mathbf Z/m)_T$, which is $M_T/mM_T$: the maps $u\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{au}$ and $\bar u\mapsto u\otimes1$ are well defined, are inverse on pure tensors, and commute with restriction, hence give inverse maps after sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Hence $M_T/mM_T\cong\mu_{m,T}$. From the tensors defining [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], associativity and $mA=0$ give
$$A(1)_T\cong M_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}A\cong(M_T/mM_T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A\cong\mu_{m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A.$$
On the etale site use the finite Tate line and its signed tensor powers of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Choose a primitive $m$-th root $\zeta\in k$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. On every $k$-scheme $T$, $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies $(\mathbf Z/m)_T$ with $\mu_{m,T}$ in both topologies: the factorization $z^m-1=\prod_a(z-\zeta^a)$ has pairwise unit differences, so every root on an object $V$ is uniquely one of the $\zeta^a$ on a clopen partition of $V$. Conversely such a locally constant choice gives a root. These descriptions commute with restriction. Thus the same root identifies $A(1)_T$ with $A_T$, and its tensor powers and dual basis identify every $A(r)_T$ with $A_T$, including $r=0$ and $r<0$. These auxiliary trivializations commute with every $k$-morphism and with coefficient maps at this common annihilating level. For a map between different finite coefficient levels, choose a common power $m$ annihilating both and its primitive root; use the compatible power of that root at a smaller exponent. The exponent-transition clause of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies these finite descriptions. They also identify the etale finite twist with its pro-etale inverse image. Only the test for invertibility uses this choice; the map being tested is always the canonical unit.

source.place: Coefficients and final twist sentence of Reduction to a geometric fibre; explicit all-n, all-signed-twist interpretation

proof.text: First compute $R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,B)$ for every finite abelian group $B$ killed by a power of $\ell$. For $B=\mathbf Z/\ell$, apply [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line](1) with $N=1$ and free coefficient module $\mathbf Z/\ell$; the root trivialization of step 1 identifies its twist with this constant sheaf, with its degree-zero isomorphism the constants map. The zero group has zero cohomology by the resolution definition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For any other $B$, argue by induction on its cardinality: choose $x\ne0$ and the least $s\geq1$ with $\ell^s x=0$. Then $y=\ell^{s-1}x$ has order $\ell$, $C=\langle y\rangle\cong\mathbf Z/\ell$, and $D=B/C$ has smaller cardinality and is still killed by the same power $\ell^a$. The exact sequence $0\to C\to B\to D\to0$, regarded as modules over the finite ring $\mathbf Z/\ell^a$, remains exact for constant sheaves by [lem-constructible-constant-exact]. We use the underlying abelian sheaves: the kernel and cokernel of a module-sheaf map carry the induced module actions, so forgetting those actions preserves this short exact sequence. Apply the long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to global sections. The vanishing for $C$ and the induction hypothesis for $D$ give $H^q(\mathbf A^1_k,B)=0$ for $q>0$ and a short exact sequence $0\to H^0(C)\to H^0(B)\to H^0(D)\to0$. In its comparison with $0\to C\to B\to D\to0$, the outer constants maps are isomorphisms. The middle map is injective because an element mapping to zero first maps to zero in $D$ and then comes from a zero element of $C$; it is surjective because a section can first be matched in $D$ and its remaining difference then lifted from $C$. Hence $B\to H^0(\mathbf A^1_k,B)$ is the constants isomorphism. The same induction proves that $|B|$ is a power of $\ell$: $|0|=1$, $|C|=\ell$, and $|B|=|C||D|$ by partitioning $B$ into the cosets of $C$. In particular this holds for the additive group of every $A_{E,n}$; no freeness of $A$ over a cyclic coefficient ring and no divisibility of $n$ by the ramification index has been assumed.

proof.text:
Let $\bar x$ be any geometric point of the arbitrary $k$-scheme $X$ and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$. The local polynomial description in [def-sbc-affine-space] makes $p$ affine: over every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. It is therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], regardless of whether $X$ is quasi-compact, separated or Noetherian. Its strict-local base change is $\mathbf A^1_S$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to the underlying torsion abelian sheaf $A$ to identify
$$(Rp_*A)_{\bar x}\cong R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_S,A).$$
This is the canonical restriction identification. On degree zero the stalk of the adjunction unit is the constants map $A\to H^0(\mathbf A^1_S,A)$: in the formula for [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] the unit restricts a locally constant section to the fibre product, and then to the strict-local limit.

source.place: Reduction to a geometric fibre: strict-henselization stalk formula; Stacks Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images

proof.text:
Write $f:\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $h:\mathbf A^1_S\to\mathbf A^1_k$ and $e:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$. The square $fh=ge$ is Cartesian. Here $f$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; $g$ is affine (source and target are affine), hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The finite additive group of $A$ has invertible order: it is killed by $\ell^n$, so its order is a power of $\ell$, whereas $\operatorname{char}k=p\ne\ell$. Thus [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] applies with its smooth side $f$ and its qcqs side $g$, and gives $f^{-1}R^qg_*A\cong R^qh_*A$. By [sbc-lem-strict-henselian-constant-cohomology], $H^0(S,A)=A$ by constants and $H^q(S,A)=0$ for $q>0$. The natural constant-sheaf identification of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], also for abelian sheaves by transporting their group operations, identifies $R^qg_*A$ with the constant sheaf of its sections over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, which are its stalk at the identity geometric point. That stalk is $H^q(S,A)$ by [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] for the qcqs $g$: the strict henselization of the separably closed field $k$ at the identity point is $k$ itself, so the fibre product is $S$. Thus $R^qg_*A$ is the constant sheaf of the groups $H^q(S,A)$. In degree zero the base-change map [sbc-def-base-change-map] carries a constant section to that same constant section, by its counit transpose formula. Therefore the canonical unit $A_{\mathbf A^1_k}\to Rh_*A$ induces an isomorphism on degree zero, and its target has zero positive cohomology sheaves; negative cohomology is zero for a sheaf's right derived direct image. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes this unit invertible. Applying derived sections and the etale composition formula (5) of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] gives
$$h^*:R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_S,A).$$
The map is pullback: the composition comparison is the canonical one, and on constants both paths send $a$ to the constant section $a$. Step 2 now implies that $A\to H^0(\mathbf A^1_S,A)$ is an isomorphism and all its higher cohomology groups vanish.

source.place: Reduction to a geometric fibre: the square with smooth side A1_k -> Spec k; Stacks Tags 0EYU and 03QO

proof.text: By steps 3 and 4, at every geometric stalk the unit $A_X\to Rp_*A_{\mathbf A^1_X}$ is an isomorphism on degree zero and both sides have zero cohomology in every other degree. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the cohomology-sheaf maps and then [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to conclude that it is invertible on the etale site. This also proves the assertion in the fixed-ring module derived category: the canonical, unit-compatible forgetful comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] identifies the underlying unit with the one just tested. Forgetting coefficients detects an isomorphism on each cohomology module sheaf (the inverse of a bijective module homomorphism is module-linear), and hence detects the required derived isomorphism. Conjugate by the sheaf trivializations of step 1. Naturality of the adjunction unit then gives precisely the same result for the canonical map $A(r)_X\to Rp_*A(r)_{\mathbf A^1_X}$, for every signed integer $r$.

proof.text:
Transport the actual unit to the pro-etale site, with constant ring $A$ and the etale finite twist as witness. Use the notation $A_T=\nu_T^*$, $l=p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$, $r=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $P=Lp_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $s=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}$, $a:A_{\mathbf A^1_X}l\cong PA_X$ and $b:A_Xr\to sA_{\mathbf A^1_X}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Its hypotheses hold because $p$ is qcqs and the input $lL$, $L=A(r)_X$, is in degree zero. By that node $b$ is an isomorphism and is the transpose of $A_{\mathbf A^1_X}(\varepsilon^e)a^{-1}$. Transposing
$$s(a_L)\circ b_{lL}\circ A_X(\eta^e_L):A_XL\longrightarrow sPA_XL$$
and using naturality of $a$ gives $A_{\mathbf A^1_X}(\varepsilon^e_{lL}\circ l\eta^e_L)$ conjugated by $a_L$, hence the identity by the etale triangle identity. This composite is consequently the pro-etale unit $\eta^p_{A_XL}$, since an adjunction transpose is a bijection. Every factor is invertible by step 5 and the cited comparison, so the pro-etale unit is invertible. Step 1 identifies its coefficient object with the specified detailed finite twist. This proves equality under comparison of the canonical unit maps, not merely existence of abstract isomorphisms of their endpoints.

source.place: Transport paragraph of lem-pur-a1-direct-image.proof.md, with named-unit verification; Stacks 099R and 0B65

proof.text: For the etale cohomology conclusion apply $R\Gamma(X,-)$ to the unit proved invertible in step 5. Its target identifies canonically with $R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_X,A(r))$. To see this at the resolution level, take a bounded-below injective resolution $I$ on $\mathbf A^1_X$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the inverse image is exact and left adjoint to $p_*$; hence $p_*$ sends an injective to an injective, since lifting a morphism into $p_*I$ along a monomorphism transposes to lifting into $I$ along its inverse-image monomorphism. Thus $p_*I$ computes both $Rp_*$ and its derived sections. The section complexes agree termwise by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $\Gamma(X,p_*I)=\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_X,I)$. The resulting map is the ordinary cohomology pullback, since the unit first pulls back sections and then maps to the resolution. It is therefore an isomorphism in every degree. For the pro-etale cohomology conclusion use the natural global comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] for both $X$ and $\mathbf A^1_X$. It applies to arbitrary schemes and degree-zero etale twists with finite ring $A$. Compatibility with pullback is the all-support case $C=X$ of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. In its commuting square the horizontal comparisons and the etale vertical pullback are isomorphisms, so the pro-etale vertical pullback is an isomorphism as well. For $q<0$ both groups are zero by the nonnegative injective resolution convention [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Consequences of the unit: derived sections, all degrees and canonical site comparison

proof.text:
The isomorphisms obtained are always the canonical pullback maps, with no chosen-root factor in their definition. Fix a $k$-morphism $v:X'\to X$. For completeness, naturality also holds for the derived units themselves. Write $w=\mathbf A^1_v$, $p'=p_{X'}$, and $L=A(r)_X$. In the etale topology let $\theta:p'^{-1}v^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}p_X^{-1}$ be the canonical inverse-image square identification and let $\beta:v^{-1}Rp_{X,*}\to Rp'_*w^{-1}$ be the exchange map of [sbc-def-base-change-map], applied with the sides of the projection square exchanged. Its transpose is $w^{-1}\varepsilon_{p_X}\circ\theta_{Rp_{X,*}}$. Consequently the transpose of
$$Rp'_*(\theta_L^{-1})\circ\beta_{p_X^{-1}L}\circ v^{-1}(\eta_{p_X,L})$$
is
$$\theta_L^{-1}\circ w^{-1}(\varepsilon_{p_X,p_X^{-1}L}\circ p_X^{-1}\eta_{p_X,L})\circ\theta_L=\operatorname{id}.$$
Naturality of $\theta$ gives the displayed equality, and the triangle identity gives its final value. The composite is therefore exactly $\eta_{p',v^{-1}L}$. Both units are invertible by step 5, so this also makes the exchange map invertible on this coefficient object. For the pro-etale etale-origin twists, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] respects the chosen square identification. Together with the named counit-mate normalization used in step 6, it identifies the two exchange maps: their adjoint transposes are the same square identification followed by the same counit. The identical unit equation follows by the injectivity of the adjunction transpose. Thus the derived-unit isomorphisms, as well as their cohomology consequences, are natural in $X$. For a $k$-morphism $v:X'\to X$, the square of projections satisfies $p_X\circ\mathbf A^1_v=v\circ p_{X'}$. The identity-and-composition clauses of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], with full support, therefore give $(\mathbf A^1_v)^*p_X^*=p_{X'}^*v^*$ in both topologies, and that node also identifies these operations under the canonical comparison. Naturality of the sheaf inverse-image unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and the functorial resolution definition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], give $p^*\circ H^q(u)=H^q(p^{-1}u)\circ p^*$ for every finite coefficient morphism $u$, including quotient coefficient maps; no tensor-exactness or flatness of such a map is used. The same statement on pro-etale sites follows either from the unit identity of step 6 or from the natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. The inverse isomorphisms inherit these commuting squares by composing with inverses. If $X$ is empty, its sheaf cohomology groups and direct-image unit have zero source and target, so that case is included.
